questions.question_text: An electric current can flow only when the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Current flows only when the circuit forms a complete path.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a source of electric energy in a simple circuit?
questions.explanation: A cell provides electric energy to the circuit.

questions.question_text: Which device is used to open or close a circuit?
questions.explanation: A switch can break or complete the circuit.

questions.question_text: A bulb glows only if current flows through its filament.
questions.explanation: The filament heats up and glows when current passes through it.

questions.question_text: The thin wire inside an electric bulb is called:
questions.explanation: The filament is the thin wire that glows when heated by current.

questions.question_text: Which material is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper allow electric current to pass through easily.

questions.question_text: Which statement about an electric cell is correct?
questions.explanation: An electric cell has two terminals, positive and negative.

options.option_text: It has a positive and a negative terminal
It is the same as a bulb

questions.question_text: What happens when a switch in a simple bulb circuit is turned off?
questions.explanation: The circuit breaks and current stops flowing.

questions.question_text: Rubber is usually used to cover electric wires because it is an insulator.
questions.explanation: Rubber does not allow current to pass through easily, so it provides safety.

questions.question_text: Why should wet hands be avoided while touching electric switches?
questions.explanation: Water can conduct electricity and increase the risk of electric shock.

options.option_text: Because water can help electricity pass and cause shock
Because wet hands cool the bulb

questions.question_text: The positive end of an electric cell is usually marked by:
questions.explanation: The positive terminal of a cell is generally marked with a plus sign.

questions.question_text: Why does a bulb not glow when there is a gap in the wire?
questions.explanation: The circuit becomes incomplete, so current cannot flow.

questions.question_text: What is an electric circuit?
questions.explanation: An electric circuit is a complete path through which electric current flows.

accepted_answers: A complete path for electric current
A path through which current flows
A closed loop carrying electric current

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an insulator?
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator and does not allow electric current to pass easily.

questions.question_text: The combination of two or more cells is called a:
questions.explanation: A battery is formed when two or more cells are connected together.

questions.question_text: Which effect of electric current makes a bulb glow?
questions.explanation: The heating effect of current makes the filament hot enough to glow.

questions.question_text: Which instrument in a house opens the circuit automatically when too much current flows?
questions.explanation: A fuse or safety device breaks the circuit when current becomes too high.

questions.question_text: Why are electric wires made of metal but covered with plastic?
questions.explanation: Metal conducts electricity, while plastic insulates and protects the user.

options.option_text: Both metal and plastic are conductors
Plastic carries more current than metal

questions.question_text: A cell has stored chemical energy that can be converted into electrical energy.
questions.explanation: Cells convert chemical energy into electrical energy in a circuit.

questions.question_text:
Assertion: A bulb will not glow in an open circuit.
Reason: Electric current needs a complete path.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.option_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true

questions.question_text: A student connects a cell, a bulb, and wires, but the bulb does not glow. What should be checked first?
questions.explanation: The most basic check is whether all connections are correct and the circuit is complete.

options.option_text: Whether the room is dark enough
Whether the circuit is complete and connections are proper

questions.question_text: If a test material allows the bulb in a tester circuit to glow, the material is:
questions.explanation: The glowing bulb shows that current can pass through the material, so it is a conductor.

questions.question_text: If the fuse of a circuit has melted, what is the safest next step?
questions.explanation: The circuit should be switched off and checked properly before replacing the fuse with the correct one.

options.option_text: Touch the wires with bare hands
Insert a thick nail in place of the fuse
Switch off the supply and replace with a proper fuse after checking
Pour water on the fuse box

questions.question_text: Why is an electric iron hot when it is in use?
questions.explanation: Current flowing through its heating element produces heat.

options.option_text: Because electric current produces heating effect
Because magnets inside it move fast

questions.question_text: Why does a fuse wire melt when too much current flows?
questions.explanation: Excess current produces more heat, and the fuse wire melts to break the circuit for safety.

accepted_answers: Excess current heats it and it melts
It melts to break the circuit when current is too high
Too much current causes heating and the fuse opens the circuit

questions.question_text: Which statement about conductors and insulators is correct?
questions.explanation: Conductors allow current to pass through, while insulators resist the flow of current.

options.option_text: Conductors allow current to pass more easily than insulators

questions.question_text: Select all materials that are generally good conductors of electricity.
questions.explanation: Most metals such as copper, aluminum, and iron conduct electricity.

questions.question_text: In a simple tester, the bulb glows faintly when a liquid is tested. What does this suggest?
questions.explanation: The faint glow suggests that the liquid allows some current to pass.

options.option_text: The liquid is definitely an insulator
The liquid conducts electricity weakly or partially
The bulb is not connected to a cell

questions.question_text: Why does connecting many appliances to one socket increase risk?
questions.explanation: Too much current may flow, causing overheating and possible damage or fire.

options.option_text: It increases light from the Sun
It reduces all current to zero
It may cause excessive current and overheating
It makes the wires longer automatically

questions.question_text: If a bulb does not glow but the cell and bulb are working properly, what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: The problem may be due to a loose or incomplete connection in the circuit.

options.option_text: The circuit may be incomplete or loosely connected

questions.question_text: Why do electricians use tools with plastic or rubber handles?
questions.explanation: Plastic and rubber are insulators that reduce the chance of electric shock.

options.option_text: To protect users from electric shock

questions.question_text: The heating effect of electric current is useful in appliances like irons and heaters.
questions.explanation: These appliances are designed to convert electrical energy into heat.

questions.question_text: Which is more suitable for wiring in circuits: copper wire or rubber strip?
questions.explanation: Copper conducts electricity well, while rubber is an insulator.

questions.question_text: Which observation best shows that current is flowing in a simple circuit?
questions.explanation: If the bulb glows, it shows that current is flowing through the circuit.

questions.question_text: State one difference between a conductor and an insulator.
questions.explanation: A conductor allows current to pass easily, while an insulator does not.

accepted_answers: Conductors allow current, insulators do not
Current passes through a conductor more easily than through an insulator
A conductor carries electricity but an insulator resists it

questions.question_text: Why does a fuse protect an electric circuit?
questions.explanation: When current becomes too large, the fuse wire melts first and breaks the circuit before serious damage happens.

options.option_text: It stores extra electricity for later use
It increases current in the wire
It breaks the circuit when current becomes too high

questions.question_text: Why is a loose connection in a circuit considered unsafe in some situations?
questions.explanation: A loose connection can cause improper flow of current, heating, and sparking.

options.option_text: Because it may cause heating or sparking
Because it stops all use of a switch forever

questions.question_text: If a wire in a bulb circuit is replaced with a plastic strip, what will most likely happen?
questions.explanation: Plastic is an insulator, so the circuit will not conduct and the bulb will not glow.

options.option_text: The plastic will act like a fuse wire

questions.question_text: Which setup is best to test whether an object is a conductor?
questions.explanation: The object should be placed in a simple circuit in place of a connecting segment and observed for bulb glow.

options.option_text: Keep it near a magnet only
Insert it in a simple test circuit and check bulb glow

questions.question_text: Select all correct statements about safe use of electricity.
questions.explanation: Dry hands, proper insulation, and correct safety devices help reduce risk.

options.option_text: Switches should be touched with dry hands
Proper fuse or safety device should be used
Metal wires should always be touched directly to test current

questions.question_text: A student connects two cells incorrectly so that the circuit does not work as expected. Which idea is most important to check?
questions.explanation: The direction of connection and correct joining of terminals matter in building the circuit properly.

options.option_text: The color of the cell wrapper
Whether the terminals are connected correctly
Whether the bulb is made of glass

questions.question_text: To compare how well different materials conduct electricity, what must be kept the same in each tester setup?
questions.explanation: The same cell, bulb, wire arrangement, and testing method should be used for a fair comparison.

options.option_text: The shape of the student’s notebook
The size of the floor tiles

questions.question_text: Why is a fuse wire made of a material that melts easily?
questions.explanation: It should melt quickly when current becomes too high, so the circuit breaks before damage occurs.

accepted_answers: So it can melt and break the circuit when current is excessive
It protects the circuit by melting first
It opens the circuit during overcurrent

questions.question_text: Why does the filament of a bulb become white-hot but not the connecting wires outside?
questions.explanation: The filament is thin and designed to heat up strongly when current flows, while external wires are thicker and carry current more safely.

options.option_text: Because the outside wires do not carry current
Because the filament offers more resistance and gets heated strongly
Because the bulb glass pushes heat into the wire

questions.question_text: Why is testing an unknown object directly in a high-voltage household socket dangerous?
questions.explanation: High-voltage sources can cause serious electric shock and should not be used for informal testing.

options.option_text: Because it changes plastic into glass
Because it can cause dangerous electric shock
Because it always melts the object instantly
Because household electricity cannot light bulbs

questions.question_text: If the filament inside a bulb breaks, what will happen in the circuit?
questions.explanation: The circuit inside the bulb becomes incomplete, so current stops and the bulb does not glow.

options.option_text: The cell will become a conductor
Current will bypass the filament automatically

questions.question_text: Which option correctly matches device and function?
questions.explanation: A switch opens or closes a circuit, a cell provides electrical energy, and a bulb converts electrical energy into light and heat.

options.option_text: Cell - opens circuit; Bulb - stores current; Switch - glows
Switch - opens/closes circuit; Cell - source of electric energy
Bulb - insulates wire; Switch - makes metal
Fuse - generates electricity in the cell

questions.question_text: Which observation best supports that a liquid can conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: If current passes through a test circuit containing the liquid and the indicator responds, the liquid conducts.

options.option_text: The liquid has a bright color
The tester bulb or indicator shows current passing through it

questions.question_text: Two wires are used in different circuits. One has damaged insulation and one has intact insulation. Which is safer and why?
questions.explanation: The wire with intact insulation is safer because the insulating cover reduces risk of accidental shock.

options.option_text: The damaged one, because current escapes easily
The intact one, because insulation prevents accidental contact

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly connects conductors, insulators, and circuit safety?
questions.explanation: Conductors are used to carry current, while insulators are used to cover conductors and protect users.

options.option_text: Insulators are used to carry current and conductors are used for safety cover
Both conductors and insulators should let current pass equally
Conductors carry current and insulators help prevent shock
Circuit safety improves when bare metal is exposed
